subject: MAP & evaluation plan — pricing, burst caps, and close timeline
body:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP & evaluation plan — pricing, burst caps, and close timeline

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation I put together an initial mutual action plan (attached) that ties the evaluation milestones to commercial milestones so procurement can map sign-off and budget approvals to tangible checkpoints. The short version:

- Pilot (2 weeks): integration + small-scale eval (safety + latency checks).
- Extended eval (6 weeks): workload-shaped traffic, automated eval sets, compare quality against internal baseline.
- Commit & ramp (quarterly commit): customer signs a 6-month reserved commit that unlocks production SLAs and a committed unit price.

Open items I want to confirm with you so we can finalize legal language / procurement asks:
1) Burst capacity during ramp: do you expect short-term spikes above committed throughput in the first 60–90 days? If so, what % headroom should we plan for?
2) Overage charging during ramp: do you want pre-agreed overage caps (e.g., capped at a discounted overage rate for X% above commit for Y days) or full list overage pricing from day one?
3) Close timeline: what is your internal approval ETA for a commercial decision and the procurement signatory? Tom was mentioned as the final approver — can you confirm.

I attached the MAP spreadsheet (ranges populated), our current rate card, and a one-page SLA table. For clarity on pricing: the rate card shows committed pricing at $5.50 per 1M tokens for the model family you tested. Standard overage (no commit) is $8.00 per 1M. We frequently offer a transient overage discount during ramp for customers that commit earlier — I outline a few options in the attached MAP.

Please reply with the answers to 1–3 and any additional commercial constraints (e.g., PO timelines, required formatting for invoices). If you're happy, I can turn the MAP into a short commercial term sheet and loop in procurement.

Thanks,
Diego
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20250830_ACME_MAP_v2.xlsx (MAP workbook, milestone dates/pricing scenarios), Redwood_Ratecard_Q325.pdf (rate card snapshot), MAP_SLA_Table.png (summary)

---

From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acmehealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Barnes <tom.barnes@acmehealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-08-30T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP & evaluation plan — pricing, burst caps, and close timeline

Thanks Diego — useful summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

1) Burst behavior: yes — we expect burstiness during integration and early production (roughly 30–40% spikes above steady-state for short windows, ~minutes). We can try to smooth traffic but prefer safety margin on the vendor side.
2) Overage charge: procurement prefers a capped overage for the first 60–90 days of ramp rather than open-list billing. If you can provide a capped discounted overage (or a committed buffer) that would make approvals easier.
3) Approval path: Tom is the final signer; procurement will need a commercial term sheet + SOW. Target internal procurement review: by 2025-09-08, sign-off by 2025-09-15 if numbers are acceptable.

Also, does your rate card's "burst" line mean tokens above commit are billed at the single overage rate, or are there tiered buckets? And can you confirm whether burst credits (if granted) are consumed before any overage billing?

Appreciate the quick follow-up — happy to hop on a 20-min call if helpful.

Best,
Sarah
Director of AI Platform
Acme Health

---

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Barnes <tom.barnes@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2025-08-31T08:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP & evaluation plan — pricing, burst caps, and close timeline

Sarah — thanks, super helpful. Answers inline below and a firm proposal at the bottom:

Q: Is burst billed at a single overage rate or tiered?
A: We support both approaches operationally, but our standard public rate card is a flat overage rate ($8.00 per 1M tokens). For deals where customers commit, we can introduce a transient tiered/discounted overage structure during ramp.

Q: Are burst credits consumed before overage billing?
A: Yes — if we agree to provide a "burst buffer" (pre-approved X% of committed capacity for a defined window), that buffer is applied first. Once the buffer is exhausted, overage billing starts at the agreed overage rate for the remainder of the billing period.

Proposal (recommended, to unblock procurement quickly):
- Commit: 6-month reserved capacity of 25M tokens/month at $5.50 per 1M.
- Ramp buffer: 25% burst buffer for the first 90 days after go-live (applies to total tokens/month). Buffer is consumed before overage billing.
- Transient overage rate during buffer exhaustion: $6.50 per 1M (discounted from list $8.00) for any consumption that exceeds commit+buffer in the 90-day window.
- Post-buffer overage rate: $8.00 per 1M thereafter.
- Early-commit incentive: if the signed commitment and PO are received before 2025-09-10, apply a 10% one-time credit on the first invoice (applies to committed usage only).

Example math (month 1):
- Commit: 25M tokens at $5.50 => $137.50
- Allowed buffer (25%): 6.25M tokens applied first
- If usage = 33M tokens, excess after buffer = 1.75M => billed at $6.50 per 1M => $11.375 additional

If this sounds right I can add the exact clause language into the term sheet and produce a short schedule for procurement (MAP with milestone dates + DocuSign link). I copied Monica and Tom so procurement has the financial language on record.

Thanks,
Diego

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-09-01T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: MAP & evaluation plan — pricing, burst caps, and close timeline (internal notes)

Internal note — capturing margin and concession trade-offs before we send the final term sheet to Acme:

- 25% burst buffer for 90 days is okay, margin holds up at $6.50 transient overage if the customer signs the 6mo commit.
- If we want to be more competitive we could offer 30% buffer for first 60 days, but need to tie to an earlier signature date and require minimal 3-month ramp commit minimum. That increases downside if they overshoot immediately.
- Recommend keeping the early-commit 10% first-invoice credit but cap total concession value to no more than ~8% of expected first-quarter ARR for the deal.
- Ask legal to add a clear "buffer consumption first" clause and define how we measure token usage (UTC day boundaries, model family filtering).

I will draft the precise one-paragraph clause and hand it to Diego to include in the term sheet. Markus — want you to confirm SRE will accept the 25% burst behaviour for the live ramp (particularly the measurement method).

— Monica

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acmehealth.com>, Tom Barnes <tom.barnes@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-09-03T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Final MAP & commercial summary (next steps + DocuSign)

Sarah / Tom — following internal alignment, here is the consolidated and sign-ready plan. I attached the updated MAP workbook and a short commercial term sheet. Key points we agreed to:

1) Commit: 6-month reserved capacity, 25M tokens/month at $5.50 per 1M tokens.
2) Ramp buffer: 25% buffer (6.25M tokens/month) for the first 90 days after go-live. Buffer is applied before any overage billing.
3) Transient overage (during buffer exhaustion window): $6.50 per 1M tokens.
4) Post-buffer overage: $8.00 per 1M tokens.
5) Early-commit incentive: 10% credit applied to the first invoice if signed and PO received by 2025-09-10.
6) Measurement & billing: tokens measured per UTC billing day; model family filter applied per the scoped models in the SOW (see MAP workbook).

Next steps:
- I uploaded the term sheet and MAP to the shared Drive (link below) and created a DocuSign envelope for the commercial schedule. If procurement is comfortable, target to sign by 2025-09-10 to secure the early-commit credit.
- I'll coordinate SRE to confirm the measurement hooks and ensure usage reporting in the console is enabled for your team during the eval.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=drivefile123
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/envelopes/ENVELOPE-ACME-547

If Tom or procurement want edits to the exact buffer wording, let me know and I'll feed into legal — otherwise I can send the envelope for signature today.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to getting Acme live.

Diego
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20250830_ACME_MAP_v2.xlsx, Redwood_Ratecard_Q325.pdf, MAP_SLA_Table.png
